name: Newlyn Art Gallery
funding: Arts Council England and Cornwall Council together give 50 percent. Its support page also shows Bloomberg Philanthropies, Headley Trust, Linbury Trust, Wolfson Foundation, Ashden and DASH.
watch: 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026. No campaign targets Newlyn.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, funders show as undated logos with no readable names, and trustees are listed.

name: PICA Perth
funding: Revenue A$2.84M and 169,720 visitors (2024). WA Government through DLGSC with Lotterywest, Creative Australia, City of Perth and Minderoo Foundation, which backs Hatched and two staff roles.
watch: Minderoo holds the Forrests' $5B Fortescue gift. On 12 May 2026 the Federal Court ordered Fortescue to pay the Yindjibarndi $150M for Solomon Hub.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2006 with financial statements, a named 2024 donor list and partners, and names its directors.

name: PICA Portland
funding: $2.5M expenses (FY2025). Oregon Arts Commission, City of Portland, Warhol, Ford, Mellon, Meyer Trust and Kinsman foundations; Nike, Netflix, Google. Pacific Power Foundation and NW Natural also give.
records_note: Posts a 2025 impact report and names its board, with sponsor logos for the 2026 TBA festival; Form 990s for 2002 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: €14.8M annual budget, 950k park and gallery visitors. Fundação de Serralves endowment, Portuguese Ministry of Culture, and Porto Municipality.

name: Glenstone
watch: Mitchell Rales co-founded Danaher. A 2015 Senate inquiry examined 11 private museums, Glenstone among them, over founders' tax benefits.
records_note: No annual reports, donor list or board on its site; Form 990-PF filings for 2006 to 2024 are public on ProPublica.

name: MacKenzie Art Gallery
funding: Canada Council, Saskatchewan Arts Board, City of Regina, Sask Lotteries. 2024-25 corporate sponsors: TD Ready Commitment ($200k+), Rawlco Radio, RBC Foundation, Canada Life, SaskTel.
watch: TD Bank, the largest corporate sponsor, pleaded guilty on 10 October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, with about $3B in penalties.
records_note: Posts annual reports and signed financial statements for each year from 2014-15 to 2025-26, names sponsors and donors in the 2024-25 report, lists trustees.

name: Fondation Beyeler
funding: CHF 30M budget. Basel-Stadt and Riehen give about 9%; the Beyeler Foundation covers a 27% deficit. Sponsors include UBS (Artist Talks) and Globus.
watch: UBS paid a $100M US Federal Reserve fine in 2004 for dollar trading with Iran and other sanctioned countries.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; sponsors appear as unlabelled undated logos, and the team page does not list a foundation board.

name: Castello di Rivoli Museo d Arte Contemporanea
funding: €6.5M. Regione Piemonte, Città di Torino, Fondazione CRT, Compagnia di San Paolo.

name: MAXXI
funding: Ministry of Culture EUR 14.0M in 2025, Regione Lazio 350k, Enel 600k as a promoter member, sponsors KME and Bulgari. Eni pays EUR 48,750 for archive work.
watch: On 27 October 2025 six artists withdrew and six collectives called a boycott over Eni, Leonardo and Gaza. MAXXI's 2025 accounts show no Leonardo money.
why_flagged: Ministry of Culture EUR 14.0M in 2025, Regione Lazio 350k, Enel 600k as a promoter member, sponsors KME and Bulgari. Eni pays EUR 48,750 for archive work.
records_note: It posts yearly accounts for 2020 to 2025 with a management report and names its board, but sponsors are undated logos.

name: Wattis Institute
funding: Part of California College of the Arts. Donate page lists the Horace W. Goldsmith and Richard foundations, San Francisco Grants for the Arts, and individual donors.
watch: Non-profit research institute and contemporary gallery at CCA.
records_note: No records of its own; parent CCA lists trustees and files 990s on ProPublica, and the Wattis donate page names supporters undated.

name: SITE Santa Fe
funding: No funder list is published. Its Business Council lists local galleries, hotels, distilleries and Century Bank. FY2024 revenue was $6.5M, with $4.2M in contributions.
watch: Board includes Louisa Stude Sarofim and Carl Thoma. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found, but no funder list exists to test.
records_note: It names 15 trustees and 10 advisers, benefit sponsors by tier for July 2026 and 31 Business Council firms; ProPublica holds Form 990s to 2024.

name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
funding: Nubank (R$10M a year to 2027, about 40% of budget), Bradesco, Motiva, Instituto Votorantim, Bloomberg, Usiminas and others. 98% of funds come through the Rouanet tax law; free entry.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies faces a May 2026 UK artists' letter to five London theatres over Israel; no action is aimed at Tomie Ohtake.
records_note: Posts balance sheets for 2023 and 2024 and names its three governing bodies; sponsors appear as tiered logos with no date, and no annual report.
